name: Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg and Related Groups of Monuments
description: Saint Petersburg, in northwestern Russia, was laid out from 1703 by Peter the Great as a grand new capital on the water. Its canals and more than 400 bridges earned it the name "Venice of the North." Walking the centre, you pass Baroque and neoclassical landmarks such as the Winter Palace, the Hermitage and the Admiralty. The city was later renamed Leningrad and became closely tied to the October Revolution.
